title: Foreign Workers (Prohibition of Unlawful Employment and Assurance of Fair Conditions) Law, 5751-1991
amended: amended several times (consolidated English text undated)
source_tier: Secondary (UNHCR Refworld; unofficial English translation of a consolidated version)
site_status: NEW: add to national-laws (already cited in the domestic-workers database as Foreign Workers Law, 1991)
note: Checked on 2026-11-21 against the Refworld PDF supplied by IMR (unofficial English, consolidated with later amendments, date of consolidation not stated). Known as the Foreign Workers Law. In force 1 May 1991. Employer may employ a foreign worker only with a medical certificate, a written contract in a language the worker understands (s. 1C), medical insurance (s. 1D) and suitable housing (s. 1E); deposits into a Foreign Workers Fund paid to the worker on departure (Chapter Four, s. 1K), with exemptions or reductions possible for nursing-care (caregiver) workers employed by individuals; offences and supervision in Chapter Five. title: Employment of Employees by Manpower Contractors (Application for Licence) Regulations, 5756-1996
title_original: תקנות העסקת עובדים על ידי קבלני כוח אדם (בקשה לרשיון), תשנ"ו-1996
source_tier: Secondary (israelilegislation.com, private site; unofficial English translation of the consolidated Hebrew text as of 2023-09-18)
note: Read on 2026-11-21 in the built-in browser. Only the Hebrew text in Reshumot is binding; official Hebrew text still to find (Nevo or the Knesset database). Made under ss. 2(d) and 25 of the Employment of Employees by Manpower Contractors Law, 5756-1996 (the parent Law is not yet in our tables). Licence applications to the Minister of Labour with an affidavit, office conditions (incl. a private interview room for job candidates) and the data needed to set the guarantee amount; consent to criminal-record checks of managers; decision within three months (reg. 4). The Foreign Workers Law, 5751-1991 adopts this Law's definition of 'manpower contractor'.

title: Prevention of Infiltration Law (Offenses and Jurisdiction), 5714-1954
amended: Amendment No. 3 and Temporary Order 5772-2012; Legislative Amendments and Temporary Order 2014 (and later amendments to Aug 2018)
source_tier: Secondary (UNHCR Israel; unofficial English translation, consolidated version as of August 2018)
note: Checked on 2026-11-21 against the unofficial consolidated English translation (Aug 2018) published by UNHCR Israel (link from IMR). Official Hebrew text to find on Nevo or the Knesset database. Defines an 'infiltrator' as a non-resident who entered other than through a designated border crossing (s. 1); offences ss. 2-9; presumption that anyone who entered without permission or stays unlawfully is an infiltrator (s. 10); deportation orders by the Minister of Defense (s. 30); custody, review by the Director of Border Control and release on guarantee (ss. 30A-30D); detention conditions (s. 30B); residence orders and Residency Centers (ss. 32A-32D, the 'Holot' facility). The Supreme Court struck down earlier detention provisions in Adam v. Knesset (2013), already in our decisions table (il-adam-2013).

title: Instructions No. 1 of 2026 on Recruiting, Employing and Licensing Foreign Workers in Iraq
topic: labor; work permits; recruitment; domestic workers
site_status: LEAD: official text needed before publishing
note: Described in a Baghdad law firm's article of 10 Oct 2026 (not read in the original). title: Law No. 164 of 2024 Enacting the Asylum Law for Foreigners
title_original: قانون رقم 164 لسنة 2024 بإصدار قانون لجوء الأجانب
in_force: day after publication in the Official Gazette (art. 3 of the issuing law)
source_tier: Secondary (UNHCR Refworld; Arabic text plus unofficial English translation)
note: Checked on 2026-11-21 against the unofficial English translation supplied by IMR (Refworld record 149388). Issued 16 December 2024 (14 Jumada al-Akhira 1446); executive regulations due within six months of entry into force. Creates the Permanent Committee for Refugee Affairs under the Ministry of Interior, which decides applications within six months (lawful entry) or one year (irregular entry), with priority for vulnerable applicants (art. 7); rejection leads to a deportation request. Art. 13 bans extradition or forced return of a refugee. Art. 18 right to work and to practise a profession with a permit; art. 19 self-employment and companies; art. 30 bans political, party and union activity. Art. 37: employing or sheltering an asylum seeker without notifying the police is punishable by at least six months' imprisonment and/or a fine of EGP 50,000-100,000. Gazette issue and date still to confirm.

title: Comprehensive Guide of Principles for Issuing Work Permits for Non-Jordanian Workers (edition of 28 October 2026)
title_original: الدليل الشامل لأسس إصدار تصاريح العمل للعمال غير الأردنيين
topic: work permits; closed professions; quotas; sector transfer; absconding reports; farm work; day labourers
amended: updated by Ministry resolutions, latest cited 8/2026, 23/2026 and 31/2026
note: Ministry of Labour consolidated guide, about 176 pages, with the dates of the resolutions that amended each part. Part III lists professions closed to non-Jordanians (office work, sales, hairdressing, electrical work, security guards, most education jobs); Gaza Strip residents may work as cleaners and loaders in all sectors (Resolution 8/2026). Part VI sets the ratio of Jordanian to non-Jordanian workers by sector; for farms the number follows the Ministry of Agriculture classification of the holding. Part X: domestic workers may be recruited from abroad with the Minister's approval. Part XIV: agriculture is a closed sector (a farm worker may move out only to domestic gardener work or to another farm owner); domestic workers may not change sector; day-labourer flexible permits are closed except to the specialised-skills permit. Part XIX: an employer may report a worker as absconded only after paying all social security, not in the last two months of the permit, and for no more than 10% of its workers; a false report blocks the employer and the worker gets a new permit. Part XXVI sets rules for private farm permits (Jordan Valley holdings over 3,400 m2). It also reprints Regulation 142/2019 on fees, the 2012 Instructions on employment and recruitment (art. 12: farm workers may change employer only within agriculture; art. 16: the Instructions do not apply to domestic workers or QIZ workers; art. 18 repeals the 2009 Instructions, OG 4976 of 19 Aug 2009), the 2007 QIZ Instructions, the 2020 Instructions for Syrian workers, the 2024 Principles for specialised skills, and the 2025 Principles for day-labourer free permits (JOD 800 plus JOD 50; work for any employer in the same profession, Labour Law art. 12(G)(2)). Each reprinted instrument could become its own row once its gazette details are checked.

title: Anti-Trafficking (Legislative Amendments) Law, 5766-2006 (central parts)
title_original: חוק לאיסור סחר בבני אדם (תיקוני חקיקה), התשס"ו-2006
topic: trafficking; forced labour; slavery; passport retention; victim compensation; legal aid
amended: amends the Penal Law 5737-1977 and the Legal Aid Law 5732-1972
note: Unofficial English translation of the central parts, dated 27 Sep 2006, signed by the Government Coordinator of the Battle against Trafficking in Persons, on gov.il. Passed 19 Oct 2006, in force 29 Oct 2006. Adds to the Penal Law: s. 374A kidnapping for trafficking (20 years); s. 375A holding a person in slavery, including for work (16 years, 20 for a minor); s. 376 forced labour (7 years); s. 376A holding a passport or identity document for trafficking purposes (5 years; the general offence of holding a passport goes up to 3 years); s. 376B causing a person to leave their country for prostitution or slavery; s. 377A trafficking (16 years); s. 377B minimum sentence of one quarter of the maximum; s. 377C court must give reasons for not awarding compensation; s. 377D-E forfeiture and a fund, at least half of it for victims. Legal aid for all trafficking and slavery victims, including in Entry into Israel Law proceedings. Partial translation only: the official Hebrew text in Reshumot is to be found.
